Pwned
POHND (also PWOHND)
verb (Millennial slang)
A deliberate misspelling of owned (soundly beaten, dominated), from early-2000s online gaming. The p sits beside the o on a QWERTY keyboard, and a much-repeated (unverified) legend credits a Warcraft map-maker’s typo, "has been pwned," for the form. Hacker and gamer culture kept the typo on purpose as an in-group mark; pwnage and pwn followed. In 2013 the security researcher Troy Hunt launched the data-breach checker Have I Been Pwned, which gave the word a second, more sober life: to be pwned is to have your accounts compromised.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To be pwned is to be utterly beaten, outplayed, humiliated in a game or argument; to have pwned someone is to have dominated him so thoroughly that the victory is a public mockery. In security talk it means your data has been taken. The Christian observation starts with the root word the typo hides: owned. Every person is owned by something. The gamer’s boast is that he owns his opponent; the gospel’s claim is that none of us owns himself. "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price" (1Co 6:19-20). There is a real defeat in Scripture that dwarfs every match: at the cross Christ, "having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" (Col 2:15). That is the only pwnage worth celebrating, and the victory belongs to Him. In ordinary contests, Scripture asks for a victor’s humility: "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth" (Pro 24:17). A father tells his son: win hard, lose well, and never rub a beaten man’s face in it; a gracious winner is rarer than a skilled one. And remember whose you are before you boast about whom you have beaten.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial gamer slang (early 2000s typo of owned) for being utterly beaten or, since 2013, hacked; its hidden root asks who owns us: ye are not your own, ye are bought with a price (1Co 6:20).

PWNED, v. (Millennial gamer slang, early 2000s; typo-spelling of owned) Utterly defeated, dominated, humiliated. "You just got pwned." Also pwn, pwnage.

Security sense (2013–present, Have I Been Pwned): having one’s accounts or data compromised in a breach.

Webster (1828), root own: OWN, adjective [ See Owe and Ought .] 1. Belonging to; possessed; peculiar; usually expressing property with emphasis, or in express exclusion of others. It follows my, your, his, their, thy, her. God created man in his own image. Adam begat a son in his own likeness. Let them fall by their own counsel. He washed us from our sins in his own blood. In the phrases, his own nations, his own country, the word own denotes that the person belongs to the nation or country. 2. own often follows a verb; […]

Decode for parents: the word is trash talk; the root is a catechism question — whose are you?

1Co 6:19-20 — "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's."

Col 2:15 — "And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it."

Pro 24:17 — "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:"

Rom 12:21 — "Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good."

1Jn 5:4 — "For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith."

Modern Corruption

Pwned celebrates domination and humiliation of the beaten; Scripture forbids gloating and points to the one decisive triumph, Christ’s over the powers.

expand to see more

The word carries the culture of trash talk: victory is not complete until the loser is mocked. Online, where opponents are faceless, that cruelty comes cheap, and boys learn to measure themselves by how thoroughly they can humiliate someone else. Scripture refuses the posture even toward real enemies: "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth" (Pro 24:17). The gloater is not strong; he is still hungry, needing the other man’s shame to feel his own win.

The recovery is to know the real war and the real Victor. "Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good" (Rom 12:21). The Christian does fight, but his weapons are faith and goodness, and his victory is borrowed: "whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith" (1Jn 5:4). Let the young compete with fire and lose with grace, and teach them that the most important sentence about ownership was written in blood: ye are bought with a price.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English agen (own) → gamer owned (defeated) → typo pwned (early 2000s) → 2013 security sense (data breached).

Old English agnian — to possess, to make one’s own

1990s gamer slang: owned — decisively beaten

Early 2000s: keyboard-slip pwned kept on purpose; pwn, pwnage

2013: Troy Hunt’s Have I Been Pwned — the breach sense

Biblical anchor: ye are not your own (1Co 6:19); Christ triumphing over the powers (Col 2:15)

Usage
